title: Rent, host or carry the model
brief: The model has to run somewhere, and a customer, regulator or security team will ask where prompts go and who holds the keys. Data control, traffic shape, GPU skills and the quality you need are open. Compare the places a model can run and map each data control to what it really covers.

blocks.text: Four places to run a model, and the controls around them

blocks.title: Where the model runs
blocks.intro: Microsoft advises starting with Global Standard and moving only for a specific reason such as data residency, reserved throughput or batch [[r24]].

options.name: Managed API, Global deployment
options.summary: Inference may run in any Azure region. Data at rest stays in the designated geography [[r24]].
pros: New models launch here first, at the lowest price and the broadest region coverage
cons: Default abuse monitoring is automated review with possible human review [[r22]]
options.bestWhen: Standard terms are acceptable and the lowest operations load matters.
options.avoidWhen: Contracts or regulators name where inference may run.

options.name: Managed API, Data Zone or Regional
options.summary: Data Zone types process data only within the data zone (US, EU or APAC). Standard and Regional Provisioned types stay in the customer-specified geography [[r24]].
pros: Data Zone Batch gives a 50% discount with a 24-hour target turnaround
cons: Geography-based types launch last, with no guaranteed availability date
options.bestWhen: A rule or contract names a zone or geography and you want managed operations.
options.avoidWhen: You need weights you control or an air gap.

options.name: Self-hosted vLLM or SGLang on GPUs (AKS with KAITO)
options.summary: vLLM offers PagedAttention, continuous batching, chunked prefill, prefix caching and speculative decoding [[r16]]. SGLang adds RadixAttention and compressed finite state machines for structured output [[r18]]. KAITO deploys open models on AKS and integrates vLLM [[r21]].
pros: You control weights, logs and network
High steady utilization can lower unit cost
cons: You own GPUs, scaling, upgrades and safety tooling
KAITO needs NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 8.0 or later (no T4 or V100), Azure CLI 2.76.0 or later, public Azure regions and no Windows node pools
options.bestWhen: Open or custom weights, strict control, high steady volume and GPU operations skills.
options.avoidWhen: Spiky or low volume, or no one to run GPUs.

options.name: On-device (Foundry Local, Ollama)
options.summary: Foundry Local is an on-device runtime and SDK on ONNX Runtime with an OpenAI-compatible API [[r20]]. Ollama runs local and cloud models behind OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible APIs [[r19]].
pros: Data stays on the device and it works offline
Foundry Local adds about 20 MB to an app and needs no Azure subscription
cons: Not a multi-user server: Microsoft points to vLLM or Triton for that
options.avoidWhen: Many concurrent users, or you need frontier quality.

blocks.caption: Data controls: what each lever covers and what it does not. Checked 2026-10-13.
head: Lever
What it controls
What it does not control
Check before you promise it
rows: Deployment type
Where inference may run: Global, Data Zone, Standard or Regional Provisioned [[r24]]
Retention or logging
The Developer tier is for fine-tuned model evaluation only: 24-hour lifetime, no SLA or residency guarantee
Zero Data Retention (OpenAI)
`store` on `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions` is always treated as false [[r25]]
Endpoints that are not eligible, such as threads, vector stores and fine-tuning jobs, which keep state until deleted
Needs approval. Abuse-monitoring logs are kept up to 30 days by default
Modified abuse monitoring (Azure)
Removes storage and human review for approved customers [[r23]]
Content filtering and other platform behaviour
Default is automated review with possible human review [[r22]]
Customer-managed key
Encryption of data at rest in the resource's associated storage: project artifacts, uploaded files, evaluation data [[r26]]
Model inference
Some previews lack it. Grant the managed identity key access first. Omit `keyVersion` to follow the latest version. RSA 2048 bits or more
Private endpoint and VNet
The network path. The agent client is injected into a customer VNet subnet for outbound traffic [[r27]]
Which tools work
Browser automation, computer use, image generation and Logic Apps are unsupported. Bing grounding, web search and SharePoint grounding use public endpoints [[r28]]

blocks.prompt: Flip the dials. No option wins everywhere, and the winner moves with data control and traffic shape.

blocks.takeaway: Residency usually starts with Data Zone or regional deployments before self-hosting. GPUs earn their keep only with steady volume, custom weights and skills.

blocks.title: Hosting and data control failure modes

items.symptom: A KAITO workspace will not schedule
items.cause: The VM size uses GPUs older than Ampere (T4, V100, M60, K80), or the pool is a Windows node pool, or the region is not public
items.fix: Use NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 8.0 or later and Azure CLI 2.76.0 or later. Avoid stopping and starting clusters that run active workspaces [[r21]].

items.symptom: Compliance asks for ZDR and a feature stops working
items.cause: `store` is always false under ZDR, and some endpoints are not ZDR eligible and keep state until deleted
items.fix: Design stateless calls, own conversation state yourself and check eligibility for each endpoint you use [[r25]].

items.symptom: A tool disappears after private networking is enabled
items.cause: Browser automation, computer use, image generation and Logic Apps are unsupported under isolation, and some grounding tools use public endpoints
items.fix: Check the tool matrix before choosing the isolation level [[r27]].

items.symptom: An audit finds prompts processed outside the required geography
items.cause: A Global deployment was chosen because it is the recommended default
items.fix: Pick Data Zone or regional types for regulated data and verify each deployment's type [[r24]].

items.symptom: The self-hosted cluster costs more than the API
items.cause: Utilization was assumed, and on-call, upgrades and safety tooling were left out
items.fix: Measure tokens per GPU-hour at real concurrency, add operations cost and compare with batch pricing before committing.

blocks.title: Keys protect storage, not inference
blocks.md: A customer-managed key covers data at rest in the resource's associated storage. It does not stop the provider processing prompts at inference time, and it is not a residency control. Match each requirement to the lever that actually delivers it [[r26]].

quiz.q: A contract requires inference to stay in the EU, and the team does not want to run GPUs. Which choice fits?
options: Global Standard, because Microsoft advises starting there for most workloads and it costs least
A Data Zone or regional deployment, because inference stays inside the zone or geography
A customer-managed key, because it keeps inference inside the geography
A Developer tier deployment, because it carries no extra residency charge
quiz.explain: Data Zone types process data only within the zone, and Standard and Regional Provisioned types stay in the geography. Global may run anywhere, a key does not control where inference runs, and the Developer tier has no residency guarantee.

quiz.q: Select every statement about customer-managed keys in Foundry that is true.
options: They cover data at rest in the resource's associated storage, such as project artifacts, uploaded files and evaluation data
They encrypt the model's inference computation so the provider cannot see prompts
Omitting keyVersion makes the resource follow the latest key version
RSA keys must be at least 2048 bits
The managed identity needs no key access, because Azure grants it automatically
quiz.explain: Keys apply to stored data, the latest version is followed when keyVersion is omitted, and RSA keys of 2048 bits or more are required. Keys do not cover inference, and you must grant the managed identity access to the key before enabling.

quiz.q: Match each tool to its role.

pairs.r: Multi-user GPU serving with PagedAttention and continuous batching
RadixAttention KV reuse and structured-output support
AKS add-on that deploys open models and integrates vLLM
On-device runtime and SDK embedded in an application

quiz.explain: vLLM and SGLang are serving engines with different strengths, KAITO is the Kubernetes layer that deploys them on AKS, and Foundry Local is an embedded runtime, not a multi-user server.

quiz.q: After the team disables public network access for the Foundry environment, an agent's browser automation tool stops working. What is the most likely cause?
options: The tool needs a larger model deployment than the one currently attached to the agent
The agent identity lost its role assignment
The public network settings were ignored by the portal
Browser automation is not supported under network isolation
quiz.explain: Foundry lists browser automation, computer use, image generation and Logic Apps as unsupported under network isolation. Model size and role assignments would show different errors, and the setting is not ignored.

takeaways: Map each requirement to the lever that delivers it: deployment type for inference location, ZDR for retention, keys for storage, private endpoints for the network path.
Residency usually starts with Data Zone or regional deployments, not self-hosting.
GPUs pay off with steady volume, custom weights and operations skills. KAITO needs compute capability 8.0 or later.
Foundry Local is an embedded runtime, not a multi-user server.
